scenario: [RFCS.6.8]: a recorded `FactAssert`'s `event_id` is the clause's function of the run id, the tier id and the `seq`, and of nothing else. Here the engine is given neither id, so both are empty ([NLFC.1.2]). LFST.2.2's session -- one Reading asserted, no pump -- is recorded: the assert's clock sample is the stream's first event, `ClockAdvance` at seq 0 ([LTIM.2.8.5], [LFST.7.1.3]), and the `FactAssert` follows it at seq 1. KNOWN ANSWER, computed from the clause's text with Python's `hashlib` in the build container, not by either runtime: preimage `"ds.rfcs.event_id.v1"` 1F (empty r) 1F (empty t) 1F be64(1) = 64732e726663732e6576656e745f69642e76311f1f1f0000000000000001; SHA-256 = b3dfad6fbb586927f4a356cb7c01a96783c4fda24c03c731553b125fe8a746ac; byte 6 0x69 becomes (0x69 & 0x0F) | 0x80 = 0x89, byte 8 0xf4 becomes (0xf4 & 0x3F) | 0x80 = 0xb4; so the event_id is b3dfad6f-bb58-8927-b4a3-56cb7c01a967. A derivation that hashed a separator-free preimage, dropped the literal, encoded `seq` little-endian or as text, or set no version and variant bits, records another id. `be64(seq)` is pinned below 2^32 only: a recording's `seq` counts every event from 0 ([LFST.7.1.3]), and no harness can reach 2^32 cheaply. PATH PINNED: the stamp on a recorded `FactAssert`, not a call to the helper ([STYL.5.10.8]) -- libds's `ds_rfcs_gen_event_id` (rfcs/codec.c) through pyds `Engine.record`, read back as each `FactAssert`'s message through libds's reader (`pyds.atoms`) in runner.py `_run_rfcs_roundtrip`; the Mercury runtime's `ds.rfcs.lfst_5_6_event_id`, read back as `FactAssert` field 8 in compiler/mercury/test/test_behave.m `rfcs_roundtrip_result` ([RCTS.1.2.23]).
